paragraphs: The GLA220d has been a key diesel variant in the GLA-Class range since the model's launch in 2013, spanning two generations. The X156 generation (2013-2020) uses the OM651 - a 2.1-litre four-cylinder diesel shared across many Mercedes models of that era, including the A-Class. From 2020, the H247-generation GLA220d switched to the OM607, a 1.5-litre diesel unit. Knowing which one your car has matters, because the components and known wear patterns differ - which is exactly why we confirm your exact engine by registration before quoting.
about.boldParagraph: We continue to rebuild and replace M256 engines for every GLA220D on the road.

cards.body: A 3.0-litre inline-six petrol mild-hybrid engine fitted to the GLA220D from 2023 to present. The M256 features an integrated starter-generator (ISG) and electric auxiliary compressor, making it a more modern and efficient design than the older M276 V6. We replace timing chains, bearings, water pump and gaskets as standard on every M256 rebuild.

compatibility.intro: Because the GLA220d spans two distinct engines across two generations, fitting the wrong replacement - or assuming an OM651 part will work on an OM607 car - risks a compatibility problem. Before we quote or supply anything, we confirm: - Your exact engine code (OM651 or OM607) via registration or VIN - Your generation (X156 or H247) - Drivetrain and ancillary specification - Any electronics or ECU considerations specific to your exact build
